title: The Manager Who Marked the Collateral: BlackRock’s Due Diligence, and a $2.5 Billion Gain to the Public
participants: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

extractionLoop.stage1_upfrontSkim: The mandate is the thing being extracted here, and the New York Fed names the holder: the due diligence on the assets taken from Bear Stearns "was conducted by the New York Fed’s advisors, which included its investment manager, BlackRock Financial Management Inc. and Ernst & Young."
extractionLoop.stage2_structuralCompromise: The structural feature is that a private asset manager was placed between the central bank and the collateral it was accepting. "All the assets purchased originated from the Mortgage Desk of Bear Stearns", and whether they qualified was assessed against criteria — US-domiciled, dollar-denominated, "rated investment grade, which was defined as rated BBB- or higher", whole loans "performing" — by the Fed’s own appointed advisors rather than by the Fed itself.
extractionLoop.stage3_informationFog: The ratings doing the gatekeeping were the same instrument the crisis had discredited: eligibility turned on an investment-grade rating of BBB- or higher, applied to mortgage assets in March 2008. The page records the criteria and the reviewer; it does not record the marks.
extractionLoop.stage4_monopolyWindfall: The position was durable and lucrative in reputational terms, and the public outcome was positive in financial ones: Maiden Lane LLC ran until 18 September 2018, when it "sold all remaining securities", with net proceeds and cash flow providing "a net gain of approximately $2.5 billion for the benefit of the U.S. public". The New York Fed’s loans were repaid with interest on 14 June 2012, and JPMorgan’s subordinate loan plus accrued interest by 15 November 2012.
extractionLoop.stage5_merseyWhitewash: There is no inquiry here and no finding against anyone. What exists is the Bank’s own ledger of its vehicle, published by the Bank, recording the terms it set, the advisors it hired and the money it made back. The absence of an independent valuation record is the gap the dossier names rather than fills.

closedLoopRatchet.inheritedFramework: Section 13(3) emergency lending through a special purpose vehicle, and a central bank without in-house capacity to value complex mortgage assets at speed.
closedLoopRatchet.newFrameworkCreated: The crisis-vehicle template — a limited liability company funded by a Federal Reserve loan, managed by a private investment manager, holding assets to maturity rather than selling into a falling market.
closedLoopRatchet.closedLoopRecirculation: The firm that assessed whether assets met the Fed’s eligibility criteria was also the firm managing them for the Fed afterwards, and the expertise that made it indispensable in 2008 was built on the same markets whose assets it was now marking.

decoyVsLedger.viralDecoy: That the Maiden Lane vehicles were a disguised gift — public money handed to Wall Street through a shell company, with BlackRock paid to bless the valuations and the taxpayer left holding the loss.
decoyVsLedger.whyDecoyFails: The loss did not happen, on the Bank’s own published ledger. The New York Fed’s loans to Maiden Lane LLC and Maiden Lane III LLC were repaid with interest on 14 June 2012, "the retirement of the last remaining debts owed to the New York Fed from the cris[is]"; JPMorgan’s subordinate loan was repaid with accrued interest; and when the final securities were sold in September 2018 the vehicle had produced "a net gain of approximately $2.5 billion for the benefit of the U.S. public". The BlackRock role is real and is worth naming — the Fed says so itself — but it was due diligence against stated eligibility criteria, conducted alongside Ernst & Young. What the dossier cannot do from this source is test the valuations: the page records the criteria, the reviewers and the outcome, not the marks, and no independent valuation review was read.
decoyVsLedger.documentedLedger: Maiden Lane LLC holding assets originated by the Mortgage Desk of Bear Stearns, purchased subject to eligibility criteria as at 14 March 2008: US-domiciled and dollar-denominated securities rated BBB- or higher, and performing whole loans. Due diligence on adherence to those criteria conducted by the New York Fed’s advisors, "which included its investment manager, BlackRock Financial Management Inc. and Ernst & Young". Repayment of the New York Fed’s loans with interest on 14 June 2012; repayment of JPMorgan’s subordinate loan plus accrued interest by 15 November 2012; and, on 18 September 2018, sale of all remaining securities producing a net gain of approximately $2.5 billion for the public.

citations.title: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, "Maiden Lane Transactions" — programme page, milestones and eligibility criteria
citations.quoteOrFact: Read from the New York Fed's own site. This page is the Bank's own ledger of the three Maiden Lane vehicles. ON BLACKROCK’S ROLE, stated directly: for Maiden Lane LLC, "All the assets purchased originated from the Mortgage Desk of Bear Stearns. Under the terms of the agreement with the New York Fed, the assets purchased by ML LLC from Bear Stearns had to meet certain eligibility requirements. The due diligence review of the assets for adherence to the eligibility criteria was conducted by the New York Fed’s advisors, which included its investment manager, BlackRock Financial Management Inc. and Ernst & Young." The criteria are specified: securities "had to be U.S. domiciled and issued and U.S. dollar-denominated", "rated investment grade, which was defined as rated BBB- or higher", and whole loans "had to be performing". ON THE OUTCOMES, from the milestones: "September 18, 2018: Maiden Lane LLC sold all remaining securities. Net proceeds from sales of the assets, as well as cash flow generated by ML LLC, provided a net gain of approximately $2.5 billion for the benefit of the U.S. public." "August 23, 2012: Maiden Lane III LLC sold all remaining securities. Subsequent to the repayment of ML III LLC’s liabilities to the New York Fed and AIG, net proceeds from sales of the securities, as well as cash flow the securities generated while held by ML III LLC, provided a net gain of approximately $6.6 billion for the benefit of the U.S. public." "July 16, 2012: Net proceeds from additional sales of securities in Maiden Lane III LLC enabled the full repayment of AIG’s equity contribution plus accrued interest and provided residual profits to the New York Fed. The New York Fed will continue to receive 67 percent of residual profits generated by future sales of ML III LLC assets." "June 14, 2012: Maiden Lane LLC and Maiden Lane III LLC repaid the loans made by the New York Fed, with interest. The successful repayment of the loans marks the retirement of the last remaining debts owed to the New York Fed from the cris[is]." "November 15, 2012: Net proceeds from additional sales of securities in Maiden Lane LLC enabled the full repayment of the subordinate loan made by JPMorgan Chase & Co. plus accrued interest." "November 12, 2014: The legal existence of Maiden Lane II LLC and Maiden Lane III LLC was formally terminated." WHAT THIS PAGE DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and it matters: it is a record of the vehicles’ structure, eligibility criteria and eventual financial outcome. It does not address the prices at which ML III acquired CDOs from AIG’s counterparties, and therefore neither supports nor refutes the contested claim that those counterparties were made whole at or near par. No SIGTARP report, congressional report or AIG counterparty schedule was read for this dossier.
